10.1002_adfm.202531993: Developing efficient and robust catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is crucial for advancing proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE). However, the benchmark iridium oxide (IrO 2 ) catalysts remain limited by their high cost and low activity under practical conditions. Herein, we report an iridium (Ir)‐based heterostructured catalyst co‐doped with high‐valent tungsten (W) and molybdenum (Mo) atoms on a strongly coupled IrCuO x /MnO 2 framework (W/Mo–IrCuO x /MnO 2 ). Using a modified molten‐salt method, W/Mo dopants are incorporated into IrCuO x /MnO 2 nanosheets, leading to optimized electronic structure and enhanced active‐site exposure. The resulting W/Mo–IrCuO x /MnO 2 exhibits a low overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in 0.5 m H 2 SO 4 and delivers a high mass activity of 1083 A g Ir −1 . Remarkably, the catalyst exhibits exceptional durability, maintaining for 400 h at 50 mA cm −2 . Additionally, the nanosheet catalyst maintains long‐term PEMWE performance (>500 h @ 1 A cm −2 at 80°C). Operando spectroscopy and theoretical calculations reveal that co‐doping high‐valent W and Mo significantly enhances the Ir oxidation state and modulates Ir─O coordination at the W/Mo–IrCuO x /MnO 2 interface, which generates optimized active sites and accelerates OER kinetics. These findings offer a promising strategy for designing high‐performance, cost‐effective OER catalysts for acidic water electrolysis.
10.1002_smll.202508852: Rapid industrialization and unlimited human activities have led to severe environmental challenges, particularly water contamination by persistent organic pollutants, posing serious risks to ecosystems and human health. Photocatalytic technology offers a sustainable remediation for pollutant degradation using solar energy. In this study, ultrathin carbon‐encapsulated ZnO nanoparticles, ZnO@C are employed, as an efficient photocatalyst, using methylene blue and methyl orange as model pollutants. The carbon has a favorable band alignment with ZnO for efficient charge transfer. In fact, the optical absorption studies and finite‐difference time‐domain simulations establish an enhanced absorption and light–matter interaction upon thin uniform carbon encapsulation. Photoluminescence quenching (≈80%) indicates reduced electron–hole recombination, facilitated by defect‐induced charge transfer from ZnO to carbon. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements identify superoxide radicals (O 2 • − ) as the dominant reactive species, driving a selective radical‐mediated degradation pathway. Compared to pristine ZnO, the ZnO@C system exhibits over 60% higher degradation efficiency. Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry analyses elucidate the sequential degradation pathway driven by O 2 • − . The ZnO@C demonstrates excellent photostability and reusability across multiple cycles, with a sixfold increase in kinetic rate constants over pristine ZnO. These improvements highlight the potential of ZnO@C core@shell nanostructures for sustainable environmental remediation.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.124690: Tire microplastics (TMPs) are abundant in urban runoff and introduce physical and chemical stressors to wastewater biocenoses. In this study, aerobic granular sludge was exposed to high TMP concentrations, intentionally selected to elucidate the mechanisms underlying microbial and functional responses, and microbial activity was quantified by respirometry alongside RNA-sequencing-based metatranscriptomic profiling. Exposure to TMPs did not impair overall wastewater treatment performance. Nitrification efficiency increased from 82.6 ± 3.2% in the control reactor to 96.7 ± 0.5% under TMP exposure, whereas total extracellular polymer substances (EPS) content decreased by more than 40%. With TMPs in the influent, the total oxygen uptake rate (OUR) increased up to 5.5-fold, while nitrifier-specific OUR rose at 50 mg TMPs/L but declined at 100–500 mg TMPs/L despite enrichment of nitrification genes, suggesting a TMP-associated decoupling between transcription and respiratory activity. TMPs exposure increased the abundance of Chloroflexota from 0.5% to 1.6% and enriched genera associated with xenobiotic degradation, EPS production and nitrogen transformations such as e.g. Pseudomonas (1.14–2.33%), Micavibrio (0.75–2.83%), Accumulibacter (0.02–1.38%), Zoogloea (0.09–1.13%) or Candidatus Nitrotoga (0-0.45%). Metatranscriptomic analysis indicated that bacterial communities underwent significant metabolic reprogramming to counteract environmental stress, optimize energy production, and switch to alternative carbon and electron flux strategies. TMPs favoured classical and complete nitrification (comammox) in granules. Bacteria downregulated denitrification gene transcription while concomitantly upregulating genes involved in xenobiotic degradation functions, reflecting an adaptive mechanism that prioritizes the removal of toxic compounds to ensure survival. The results indicate that exposure to TMPs acts as a selective pressure, reducing community diversity while favoring the proliferation of stress-tolerant microorganisms. The findings of this study provide insight into how TMPs may influence key nitrogen cycle processes in engineered wastewater bioreactors.
10.1029_2026wr043887: Kinematic wave models are widely used to represent hillslope runoff in distributed hydrological models. However, their simplified descriptions often prevent the effective use of observed soil hydraulic parameters during calibration. To address this limitation, we derived a new analytical storage–runoff relationship that explicitly incorporates percolation under wet‐soil conditions and rapid drainage through subsurface pipes. This relationship was formulated using an approximate quasi‐steady‐state solution of the vertical Darcy equation, enabling computationally efficient evaluation without vertical discretization. Integrated into a kinematic wave framework, the new formulation was implemented in a distributed rainfall‐runoff model and tested using flood events in a steep mountainous dam basin in Japan. Constraining the calibration with locally observed soil hydraulic parameters used as reference values allowed the model parameters to remain within realistic and observationally consistent ranges. This approach accurately reproduced flood hydrographs while reducing parameter and predictive uncertainty. Leave‐one‐out cross‐validation further demonstrated improved performance in simulating unobserved flood events. By improving the process representation of hillslope runoff, the proposed model allows calibration to converge toward soil parameters within observationally reasonable ranges, thereby reducing equifinality without compromising simulation performance.
